title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Variation, Environment and the Chi-Squared Test
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 6 · 11 questions · 76 marks · 30 parts · roughly an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

This cluster is two halves that pull in opposite directions. LOs 2(bb) and 2(cc) are the only essay-shaped material in Book 6, and all nine essay-scale stems in the school the papers sit here. LO 2(dd) is the second of the Book's two big methods, and it is marked step by step. Questions 1 to 5 execute a method. Questions 6 to 11 argue. Run them as two different kinds of session.

Data-led questions are the point here, not a compromise. In every other cluster a read-off-the-graph question would waste your time. In this one, handling the data is the learning outcome: LO 2(dd) is a calculation and LO 2(cc) is read off a frequency distribution.

Question 1 is the full-cycle question and it is the official one. 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 4, parts (c) and (d), at their real 6 marks, with the paper's own Table 4.1, Table 4.2 and Table 4.3 reproduced as images. Expected numbers, then the two missing cells, then the sum, then the conclusion. The specimen's parts (a) and (b) are the anchor of the Cluster 2 drill, so between the two drills you have the whole of the only extended Book 6 question that exists on an official paper.

Read section G of your study sheet before you start. You have a documented gap in this cluster and it has a real cause. The 9477 syllabus and the specimen both print v = c − 1, where v is the degrees of freedom and c is the number of classes. Your notes print df = n − 1, where n means the number of classes. But in the official symbol key n is the sample size, the number of observations. The same letter means two different things. On the specimen's maize question the school habit turns v = 3 into v = 379, which is not a row on any printed table, and the conclusion mark goes with it. An examiner comment names exactly this: candidates cited an incorrect critical value from the table due to the wrong degrees of freedom, or gave contradictory statements, and lost credit. Write v = c − 1 and say "classes" out loud as you write it. Question 2 makes you do it at c = 6 and at c = 2, and Question 3 at c = 3, precisely because the four-class case is the one you have practised.

Nothing here is a memory test. The syllabus states that candidates are not expected to remember the equations or what the symbols stand for, and that they will be given the equations, the meaning of the symbols, a t-table and a chi-squared table. What is tested is judgement: which test, how many classes, which row, which column, and what the verdict means biologically. It also states that chi-squared tests will only be expected on one row of data, so contingency tables are out entirely.

Three wording rules govern every conclusion in this drill. Say "do not reject H0", never "accept H0", because every scheme in the papers words the negative branch that way. "Due to chance" on its own is explicitly rejected, twice, in the words reject "due to chance" alone and reject "due to chance" on its own; the accepted form is the full probability sentence. And the biological conclusion is a separate mark from the statistical one, so stopping at "not significant" leaves a mark on the table.

Four real figures. Three are the specimen's own tables, so you are working off the exact layout you will meet in November, including its printing discrepancy: Table 4.1 gives the two yellow classes as 65 and 21 while Table 4.2 gives them as 55 and 31. Complete the table you are told to complete.

Cumulative over Clusters 1 and 2 and Books 2 and 3. Q3 needs the 9 : 3 : 4 epistatic merge from Cluster 2 before you can compute a single expected number. Q4(a) and Q5 need linkage as the biological conclusion. Q11 needs everything: crossing over, independent assortment, random fertilisation, dominance, codominance, linkage, sex linkage and epistasis in one answer.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as for duplicated labels. Q1 the official chi-squared, end to end · Q2 degrees of freedom at six classes and at two · Q3 chi-squared on an epistatic ratio, where the merge fixes c · Q4 both branches of the conclusion, and which test to reach for · Q5 the MCQ that fuses the verdict with the linkage diagnosis · Q6 classifying four named traits from the evidence in front of you · Q7 the systematic nine-axis comparison · Q8 polygenic inheritance in the exact wording the schemes accept · Q9 the environment named and its mechanism given · Q10 genetically identical individuals that still differ · Q11 the whole Book in one answer. Q6 and Q7 are not the same question. Q7 wants the general table of axes with an explanation attached to each. Q6 wants you to read a specific stimulus and cite the specific evidence in it, which is where the examiner comment says candidates lose the marks. Q7 and Q11 are not the same essay either: Q7 is continuous against discontinuous, Q11 is how any combination of phenotypes arises at all.

Nothing from Books 7 to 9. Natural selection, evolution and the Hardy-Weinberg equation are Core Idea 4 and none of them is needed, even in the two essays. The phenotypic variance equation VP = VG + VE is not in the learning outcomes and does not appear. Neither do standard deviation, error bars, rates, dilution series or microscopy calibration, which belong to the Mathematical Requirements and Paper 4 rather than to LO 2(dd); the one piece of that material kept is reading a p value off published data, which the specimen asked for and which Q4(d) tests.
